acceptance: In a project window the place menu offers Home, this computer and the account's spaces with a way to start one, then the account and Settings, and nothing about the folder; Home goes Home and a place opens the Homepage on it; signed out it offers this computer and Sign in. With the project rail on, the Header keeps the place alone.

The place button says this computer, the folder's path and its Cloud link or what is wrong with it; a Cloud folder by its organization until its space is known, then by the space (the account's own one is Personal) and the account's role; a folder's link is kept only while Cloud is on and only as its Cloud copy; a local place is the folder that holds it, shortened to its root and last folders, and a blank organization is no place.

A collapsed Explorer gets one Header action that expands it, beside the project; an open one gets none, even in a compact window. With the editor's tabs in the Header the project button still opens its menu beside them, and without them there is no tab column. The project rail sits below the full-width Header.

reason: TS keeps shell navigation the product does not show on macOS: a Header Home button only its smoke harness passes (ProjectShell onGoHome), sidebar top and rail navigation that no surface mounts, and the sidebar footer navigation (Changes, Settings, Feedback, Plugins) that shows only off macOS (sidebarFooterVisible). The native frontend is macOS-only: Home is in the place menu, Changes and the Agent in the Header, Settings in the application menu.

acceptance: The Agent entry is introduced once (without opening the sidebar, and not while the Agent is open); Changes waits for a first edit in a clean workspace (an already dirty one, or switching to one, is no edit) and queues behind the Agent; the always-show experiment replays both without consuming progress; a dismissal is stored and Escape acknowledges the introduction wherever focus is; malformed stored progress reads as not seen.
